questions.stem: How is auxin used in agriculture to promote plant propagation?

options.text: It is injected into seeds to speed up germination
It is sprayed on crops to kill weeds
It is applied to stem cuttings to stimulate root growth
It is added to soil to increase nitrogen levels

questions.explanation: Rooting powder contains synthetic auxins. When applied to plant cuttings, the auxin stimulates the growth of adventitious roots, allowing gardeners and farmers to clone plants from cuttings rather than growing from seed.

They prevent all plants from absorbing water
They contain synthetic auxins that cause broadleaved weeds to grow too fast and die
They attract insects that eat the weeds

questions.explanation: Selective weedkillers contain high concentrations of synthetic auxins that are absorbed by broadleaved weeds (but not narrow-leaved crops like grass). The auxin causes uncontrolled, rapid growth that kills the weeds while leaving crops unharmed.

questions.stem: How is ethene used commercially in the fruit industry?

options.text: To prevent fruit from growing too large
To change the colour of fruit permanently
To make fruit taste sweeter
To control the ripening of fruit during transport and storage

questions.explanation: Fruit can be picked unripe for transport (reducing damage) and then exposed to ethene gas at the destination to trigger ripening. This allows fruit to be shipped long distances and ripened just before sale.

questions.stem: What is the commercial use of gibberellins in brewing?

options.text: To kill bacteria in the brewing process
To increase the alcohol content
To flavour the beer
To speed up seed germination and starch breakdown in barley

questions.explanation: In brewing, gibberellins are used to stimulate the germination of barley seeds, triggering the production of amylase enzymes that break down starch into maltose. This sugar is then fermented by yeast to produce alcohol.

questions.stem: How can gibberellins be used to produce seedless fruit?

options.text: By making the seeds too small to notice
By stimulating fruit development without the need for fertilisation
By killing the seeds after they form
By preventing pollination from occurring

questions.explanation: Gibberellins can stimulate the development of fruit without fertilisation occurring (parthenocarpy). This means the fruit grows and develops normally but without seeds forming inside, producing seedless varieties like seedless grapes.

questions.stem: Which plant hormone can be used to delay the ripening of fruit and extend shelf life?

options.text: Ethene
Gibberellin
Abscisic acid
Auxin

questions.explanation: Abscisic acid can be used to slow down ripening and promote dormancy, helping to extend the shelf life of harvested fruit. Conversely, ethene is used to speed up ripening when fruit needs to be sold quickly.

questions.stem: Why might a farmer use auxin-based weedkiller on a cereal crop field?

options.text: To kill narrow-leaved grasses competing with the crop
To improve the nutritional value of the cereal
To kill broadleaved weeds without harming the narrow-leaved cereal crop
To make the cereal plants grow taller

questions.explanation: Cereal crops are narrow-leaved (monocots) and absorb less of the synthetic auxin weedkiller. Broadleaved weeds (dicots) absorb much more, causing them to grow uncontrollably and die. This selectively removes weeds while keeping the crop healthy.
